key_insight: A large-language-model screening workflow can feasibly flag potential treatment injuries from discharge summaries for clinician review, but many signals still need adjudication.
clinical_relevance: This approach may help hospitals surface previously missed inpatient harms for possible ACC consideration, supporting safer follow-up and reporting workflows.
method: Single-site, six-month pilot at Wairarapa Hospital using all 2,642 inpatient discharge summaries.
LLM generated structured harm signals with supporting text and certainty labels.
Clinicians reviewed flagged cases and decided whether escalation was warranted.
evidence_signal: The system flagged 237 cases (9.0% yield); clinicians confirmed 102 as iatrogenic harm and judged 43 more as possible harm, with 4.6% unsupported outputs.
watch_item: Results come from one hospital and clinician review without an independent chart-review gold standard, so accuracy and equity effects remain uncertain.
paper_title: AI-assisted identification of potential treatment injury from inpatient discharge summaries: an early-stage sociotechnical evaluation in a New Zealand district hospital
